coverage_note: Five Thailand consumer clusters: Koh Samui/Gulf, Phuket/Andaman (+ Ko Lanta), Bangkok river tier, Eastern Seaboard (Pattaya/Koh Samet/Bangkok gateway), and Royal Coast (Hua Hin/Cha-Am cross-Gulf). Economics cascaded 2026-06-24 on 26 Pioneer-II corridors.

partner_context.their_ambition: Grab Thailand owns the country's in-app demand — ride, food, and payments — and is pushing into premium, differentiated tiers beyond the road.
partner_context.their_pressure: Thailand's Gulf islands, Andaman resort flows, and Bangkok river traffic are high-value surfaces no super-app serves on the water — left entirely to weather-fragile diesel ferries.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: A Grab-branded foiling water tier across the Samui triangle, Phuket/Andaman, and the Chao Phraya — booked in-app, premium-priced, on sealed Atlas geometry with 15 corridors live today.

hero.title: Grab Thailand x Navier - the water layer for two coasts and a river megacity
hero.subtitle: Grab already owns Thailand's in-app demand. Water is the only transport surface no one owns yet.
hero.what_we_do_together: We launch a Grab-branded foiling water tier across Thailand's strongest water flows - the Gulf islands, the Andaman, and the Chao Phraya - booked in-app, premium-priced, and category-defining. Navier brings the software-defined hydrofoiling fleet now proven in the Maldives; Grab brings the demand, the app, the wallet.

why_now: Thailand's water flows now line up as a full network for an in-app foiling tier - a million-plus Gulf island arrivals into Samui, the Andaman's iconic island flows out of Phuket, ~40k daily Chao Phraya river trips in Bangkok, and an upper-Gulf ring linking Bangkok to Pattaya, its islands, and the Hua Hin royal coast - almost all of it inside the all-electric Pioneer II envelope today, and all still on weather-fragile diesel boats with no premium in-app water tier.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the berths and jetties already in use across Thailand's islands and rivers. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Grab Thailand owns the in-app demand in every coastal and river cluster; the water tier is the one mode no platform serves. Thailand's monsoon-fragile ferries and Bangkok's gridlock make the premium foiling layer an immediate, ownable beachhead.

network_thesis.headline: One app. Two coasts, a river, and an upper-Gulf ring. The water layer of Thailand's super-app.
network_thesis.body: Thailand is one of the most water-rich markets Grab serves - a Gulf coast of leisure islands, an Andaman coast of resort flows, a river megacity, and an upper-Gulf ring connecting the capital to the Eastern Seaboard and the royal coast - and Grab already owns the demand across all of it. The same in-app foiling tier proven in the Maldives extends cluster by cluster. Start with the Samui triangle to prove it, then the Eastern Seaboard (every leg in Pioneer II range today), the Andaman, the Bangkok river, and the cross-Gulf Royal Coast line.

markets.label: Eastern Seaboard - Pattaya, the islands & the Bangkok gateway
markets.summary: Pattaya anchors Thailand's Eastern Seaboard - Southeast Asia's largest marina (Ocean Marina), heavy daily day-trip flow off Bali Hai Pier to Koh Larn, and the national-park island of Koh Samet via Ban Phe. The Bangkok gateway ties it together: today the capital reaches Pattaya only by a 2hr-plus road slog, but the ~46 nm water line sits inside the Pioneer II envelope. This is the near-term, all-in-range cluster - every leg is a 70 nm all-electric hop today, turning a string of separate diesel ferries and a traffic-choked highway into one in-app foiling network.

hero.title: Grab x Navier - the Eastern Seaboard foiling network
hero.subtitle: Pattaya, its islands, and a clean water line back to Bangkok - all in Pioneer II range today.
hero.what_we_do_together: Grab brings the in-app day-trip and commuter demand that already flows from Bangkok down to Pattaya and out to the islands; Navier brings the silent foiling fleet. Together we replace the highway crawl and the diesel ferry queue with a premium water tier booked in the Grab app.

partner_context.their_ambition: Grab owns the on-demand and day-trip demand across the Bangkok-to-Pattaya corridor and the EEC (Eastern Economic Corridor).
partner_context.their_pressure: The Bangkok-Pattaya highway is chronically congested and the island ferries are weather-exposed diesel with no premium tier - value the platform can't capture on the road.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: A Grab-branded foiling network that links Bangkok to Pattaya by water and bundles the proven Koh Larn / Koh Samet island day-trips - the easiest near-term build because every leg is already in Pioneer II range.

markets.why_now: Bangkok reaches Pattaya only by a 2hr-plus road slog, yet the ~46 nm water line is a clean Pioneer II hop; Pattaya already moves large daily day-trip volumes to Koh Larn off Bali Hai and to Koh Samet via Ban Phe; Ocean Marina is the largest marina in SE Asia and a ready charging/berth partner; and no premium on-demand water tier exists on any of it.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the berths and jetties already in use across Thailand's coasts and islands. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Grab Thailand owns the in-app demand in every coastal and river cluster; the water tier is the one mode no platform serves. Thailand's monsoon-fragile ferries and the Eastern Seaboard's road bottlenecks make the premium foiling layer an immediate, ownable beachhead.

markets.multimodal_fit: Grab land mile to an in-city Bangkok pier -> premium foiling gateway hop to Pattaya -> in-app island day-trip to Koh Larn or Koh Samet -> Grab land mile on arrival. One booking spans the whole Eastern Seaboard.

markets.label: Royal Coast - Hua Hin, Cha-Am & the cross-Gulf line
markets.summary: Hua Hin is Thailand's historic royal-resort coast - a 15 km stretch of white sand, high-end resorts and a laid-back atmosphere ~2.5-3hr south of Bangkok, with quieter Cha-Am ~14 nm up the beach. The marquee is the cross-Gulf line: a Hua Hin<->Pattaya ferry already exists (the government-backed East-West Ferry Project, Royal Passenger Liner) because the ~58 nm water crossing cuts the 5-6hr road loop around the head of the Gulf by more than half. But it runs on slow diesel and is chronically suspended in swell. A foiling tier revives exactly the route diesel killed - and it sits inside the Pioneer II envelope today.

hero.title: Grab x Navier - the Royal Coast & the cross-Gulf line
hero.subtitle: Hua Hin and Cha-Am, and a ~58 nm foiling crossing that revives the route diesel killed.
hero.what_we_do_together: Grab brings the premium resort-coast demand and the in-app booking; Navier brings the foiling fleet that finally makes the cross-Gulf Hua Hin<->Pattaya line smooth and reliable - the leg a government ferry project proved travelers want.

partner_context.their_ambition: Grab serves the premium domestic and inbound resort demand along Thailand's royal coast.
partner_context.their_pressure: Hua Hin's high-spend guests reach Pattaya and the Eastern Seaboard only via a 5-6hr road loop; the cross-Gulf ferry that fixes it is slow diesel and chronically cancelled.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: A Grab-branded foiling cross-Gulf line (Hua Hin<->Pattaya) plus the Hua Hin<->Cha-Am coastal hop - reviving a validated, premium-priced route on a reliable all-electric platform.

markets.why_now: A government-backed Hua Hin<->Pattaya ferry (the East-West Ferry Project / Royal Passenger Liner) already proved the cross-Gulf demand - it cuts the 5-6hr road loop by more than half and is premium-priced - but it runs on slow diesel and is chronically suspended in swell; the ~58 nm crossing fits Pioneer II, and no reliable premium tier exists.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the berths and jetties already in use across Thailand's coasts and islands. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Grab Thailand owns the in-app demand in every coastal and river cluster; the water tier is the one mode no platform serves. Thailand's monsoon-fragile ferries and the Eastern Seaboard's road bottlenecks make the premium foiling layer an immediate, ownable beachhead.

markets.multimodal_fit: Grab land mile to a Hua Hin pier -> premium cross-Gulf foiling line to Pattaya (linking the Eastern Seaboard) -> Grab land mile on arrival; Hua Hin<->Cha-Am coastal hop bundles the royal-coast resorts.

proof_points.evidence: The Hua Hin<->Pattaya ferry runs under Thailand's East-West Ferry Project (Royal Passenger Liner) and cuts the 5-6hr road loop by more than half; it is already premium-priced.
proof_points.source: East-West Ferry Project / Royal Passenger Liner

proof_points.claim: Diesel is the failure mode, not the demand.
proof_points.evidence: The existing ferry is chronically suspended in Gulf swell - exactly the weather-fragility a foiling platform answers; the ~58 nm crossing fits Pioneer II.

proof_points.claim: Premium resort coast with high willingness-to-pay.
proof_points.evidence: Hua Hin's 15 km of white sand and high-end resorts anchor a premium domestic and inbound segment.

objections.objection: The Hua Hin-Pattaya ferry already failed - why try again?
objections.response: It didn't fail on demand - a government project built it because travelers want to skip the 5-6hr road loop. It fails on weather: slow diesel gets cancelled in swell. Foiling above the chop is the platform that makes the proven route reliable.

markets.the_ask: Add the Royal Coast as the marquee cross-Gulf proof: revive the validated Hua Hin<->Pattaya line on Pioneer II and bundle the Hua Hin<->Cha-Am coastal hop.
markets.end_state: A Grab-branded cross-Gulf foiling line connecting the Royal Coast to the Eastern Seaboard, with the Hua Hin-Cha-Am resort front as a premium coastal spur.
markets.close: The cleanest 'foiling fixes what diesel broke' story in Thailand: a government-proven route, premium pricing, and a crossing that fits the all-electric boat today.
